World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionRomanc.text: "I... I should probably kiss you, {name}, but I can't move a muscle. Just... give me a couple of minutes, let this sink in, and then do what you want with me!"
"Go forth, children of Golarion, and be happy! My congratulations to you both, my sincerest congratulations!"

"This was a cruel thing to do, Commander. If it weren't for the crusade... I would leave. Right now. But I have a duty to you and to the others. So I'll act like nothing happened, and stay friends with you until this war is over. But don't speak to me about love again. Ever."
"So why am I here?"
"Does the sight of a dead demon turn you on?"
"What's so special about this place? Why did you want to talk here?"
"Why would I want such a 'gift'?"
"Is it dangerous?"
"Will it make me look like a mongrel?"
"Tell me about this poison."
"Why is this so important to you?"
"A beast already lives within my soul."
"I am ready."
"No, I'm not going to poison myself."
"The pain is horrendous... in case you were wondering."
"So what will you do if I die?"
[Wink encouragingly] "If I die, you can cut off my head and claim a reward from the demons."
"How do I look?"
"I was so touched by your support... It was unusual to hear you offer up such gentle words of comfort."
"Why is there blood on my lips?"
"You kissed me? I thought you said kisses were disgusting."
"Are you really willing to change for me? Truly... I could ask for nothing more. Thank you, my love."
"What did you think of the kiss? Did you like it?"
"Let's get out of here. We still have a lot to do — the Worldwound won't defeat itself."
"I don't think I was ready for this..."
"This is nothing. I expected much worse."
"Did you really call me your 'dear one'? That's so sweet."
"I think it's time for me to say goodbye."
"This is bad, isn't it?"
"Don't worry. I'll be fine."
"Battles used to excite you, not scare you."
"It looks like you finally believe in love."
"Am I really that important to you?"
"I love you."
"So, you almost killed me..."
"You said that we share a bond. What does that mean?"
"There is no reason to be afraid. We'll survive the war together."
"I don't know what lies ahead, or what the future holds. But I know that we'll be together, no matter what happens. And if we have to face Pharasma — we'll stand before her side by side."
"What about your duty to your tribe?"
{n}The huntress's voice is a soft purr.{/n} "Alone at last."
"I am excited, but not in the way you think. I want to offer you something even more valuable than the pleasure of my touch." {n}You hear the huntress's low, sultry laugh.{/n}

"I want to offer you a gift." {n}Wenduag smiles mysteriously, and points to the demon's corpse. There is a fearsome-looking stinger at the end of his tail, and your eyes are drawn to a single bead of poison that glints dangerously at its tip.{/n} "A communion with Savamelekh's poison. It contains immense power, but it is also incredibly dangerous."
{n}The huntress points at the demon's corpse.{/n} "Because of him. This nasty scumbag called me a slave. You took his life, and now he'll have to lie there helplessly while you take his power."
"To become stronger, of course. Savamelekh gave us all a taste of his poison. That is how he shared his power with us. And right now, you need all the power you can get, right?"

"Deadly. All of Savamelekh's servants ate meat laced with his poison, but only a few of his strongest followers were allowed to experience the kiss of his sting. It was a great honor — though only a handful survived." {n}The huntress watches you closely to see your reaction.{/n}
"I don't know... You're not an ordinary mortal. Maybe the poison won't change your appearance. Why? Are you afraid you'll become... a freak?" {n}The huntress narrows her eyes.{/n}

"The poison contains Savamelekh's power. This is the poison our ancestors tasted, and they became the first of our kind. The demon gave his poison to everyone who swore to serve him. When you try it for the first time, it feels like two mad scorpions have clawed their way into your brain through your ears and have begun a fight to the death inside your head."

"Your body will start to shake violently, and you'll feel like your bones are beginning to crack and splinter. But the pain is nothing compared to the rage that will swell within your soul, a deep, dark, abiding hatred unlike anything you've ever imagined. If you survive, the agony will eventually subside, but your heart will bear the dark stain of this anger forever. With each new day, you will wake up with a single thought, a single purpose — a desire to hurt others. That is how this poison works."

"Because I'm not like you. We can keep on pretending as long as we want, but... I'm not an ordinary mortal. I was created by demons. You can turn a blind eye to the truth, but you'll never fully understand me until you become like me... at least a little. A cruel, hungry beast howls within my soul. If you do not hear its call, we can never truly be together."
"Then you have no reason to be afraid. You're a true {mf|son|daughter} of the Abyss. The poison of a demon won't kill you."

"I'll be gentle." {n}Wenduag tears the poisonous stinger from Savamelekh's tail, and brings it over to you. She caresses your skin with the stinger, delicately placing it against your chest. Then she presses down carefully until its tip pierces your skin.{/n}
{n}A look of disappointment crosses Wenduag's face. Then she shrugs.{/n} "I thought you would say that. Well, I guess this means we weren't meant to be together."
{n}A blazing inferno ignites inside you. Your body begins to spasm, and you writhe and twist in agony. You barely manage to choke back your screams of pain.{/n}

World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionRomanc.text: "Don't pass out! Talk to me! What are you feeling? Stay with me, whatever you do!"
{n}Wenduag gently strokes your cheek, and whispers softly,{/n} "I know. Hold on, dear one. You're strong. I know you can do this."

"I'll go and sabotage the war effort. I'll destroy everything you've worked so hard to build. So if you don't want me to ruin your entire campaign, you'd better not die." {n}Wenduag tries to adopt a playful tone as she teases you about the crusade, but she can't hide the worry in her voice.{/n}

{n}Wenduag tries to smile.{/n} "Right. What am I waiting for? After all, I'm sitting right next to you. I might as well stab you now." {n}Another spasm causes your body to convulse violently, and Wenduag's smile vanishes. She looks at you with an expression of sheer terror.{/n}

{n}You notice the handle of a dagger sticking out of the huntress's boot — it's the same dagger she took from the One-Eyed Devil back in Drezen. Odd... she's never carried it around with her before. She has better weapons now, weapons that are far more suitable for a serious fight... unless she simply wants to slit someone's veins.{/n}

{n}The huntress's face grows serious, and she looks you straight in the eye. She speaks quickly, as if she's afraid she won't have enough time to finish.{/n} "Remember how you told me that I was free, and that I could decide my own fate? You set me free, and that was the moment I decided I would never betray you. And I didn't! I haven't!"

World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionRomanc.text: {n}The world around you grows dim, as if you are surrounded by thick fog. You hear the sound of invisible drums, their rhythmic call beckons you — it is a call to hunt. You want to spring up and give chase. You want to catch the prey and tear it to pieces... But you are in too much pain.{/n}

{n}A new sensation washes over you — hunger. A hunger so powerful and intense, you lose track of everything else. You crave the taste of blood like an addict craves drugs. For a moment, you are so caught up in this sudden, urgent desire that you forget about the pain... and then your body contorts in another spasm of agony.{/n}

{n}You feel as though your chest is bound by invisible chains that are growing tighter and tighter by the second. You find yourself gasping for air, trying to breathe, but it's no use. The world around you grows dimmer with each heartbeat. This is it...{/n}

{n}Darkness gradually gives way to light. The pain has abated, and you are no longer in agony. Your mind grows clearer, but there's still something within you that is foul and... unnatural. You reach out with your mind, probing this dark, lingering corruption, and find that it is a source of both pleasure and disgust. It attracts and repels you in equal measure.{/n}

World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionRomanc.text: "It worked... You're still alive." {n}Wenduag, who has been staring at you worriedly, laughs in relief. Her lips are bruised and bleeding, and you taste the iron tang of blood on your lips as well.{/n}

"Not that different from before... You grew some really small horns, and of course, now you look like a rat, but I think it suits you... I'm joking, relax! Don't look at me like that!" {n}Wenduag bursts into a fit of giggles.{/n} "No, you haven't changed at all. If I had to guess, I'd say that's because Savamelekh's poison isn't strong enough to overcome your mythic power."

"I never tried to comfort you. Comforting words are for weaklings." {n}Wenduag smiles nervously.{/n} "Don't fool yourself. I'm the same wicked, lying, traitorous bitch that I was before. I still don't care about anyone but myself, but I am a little glad that you didn't just drop dead."

"But I guess you do have a point. I... I've been a real bitch, but you never stopped treating me with respect and understanding... even though I didn't deserve it. You covered for me when I made mistakes, you supported me when I felt helpless and confused... Damn, you're the first person I ever decided to be loyal to until the end!"

"I've never... loved anyone before. But if you're stupid enough to die, I'll follow you to Pharasma's judgment." {n}There's a sudden tightness in Wenduag's voice, like a bowstring stretched to its breaking point.{/n}
"I'll try. Just don't expect me to stop being a bitch overnight. This leopard will need some time to change her spots."
{n}The huntress looks away quickly.{/n} "I... I may have kissed you."

{n}You hear confusion in the huntress's voice.{/n} "I just didn't know what else to do... I remembered uplanders saying something about how a kiss could break a spell..." {n}Wenduag glances over at you in sudden horror.{/n} "That's all a load of rubbish, isn't it? Gods, what a fool I've been..."
{n}Wenduag laughs in relief.{/n} "It was absolutely horrible! I wish I had never tried it!"

"Of course. Let's go." {n}Wenduag turns to Savamelekh's corpse, and hisses spitefully,{/n} "Take a look, you winged filth. First, my lover killed you, and now {mf|he|she} has taken your power. You should never have messed with {mf|him|her}!"
{n}Wenduag looks at you sympathetically. She whispers quietly,{/n} "It's too late. There's no going back now. Hold on, dear one."
{n}Wenduag smiles affectionately as she gently strokes your cheek.{/n} "Right, and the only reason your voice is trembling is that these stones are so damn cold. Hold on, dear one."
"Can you hear me? Answer me, curse you!" {n}Wenduag's voice shakes you from your feverish, pain-filled dreams. She sounds frantic, as if she's been calling you for some time with no response.{/n}
{n}She laughs nervously.{/n} "If you die now, you'll have no one to tell except Pharasma. But if you stay alive, you can mock me to your heart's content. So just try not to die, all right?"

"Don't you dare! You hear me? Don't you dare leave me here alone! Stay awake, keep talking! You understand me, you damned uplander? Just hold on!" {n}Wenduag shakes you frantically. Her claws pierce your skin as she grasps your shoulders, but you no longer feel any pain.{/n}

{n}Wenduag's face is a mixture of horror and desperation. She stares at you helplessly, and tears fill her cat-like eyes. The world around you starts to shake. Is it an earthquake? Or has your body begun to convulse again?{/n}
"No, no, everything's fine! You're doing great. It will all be over soon." {n}Wenduag's lips tremble as she tries to hold back her sobs.{/n}
{n}Wenduag bows her head and whispers bitterly,{/n} "Don't you dare pity me... not now, when you're dying because of me!"

{n}Wenduag looks you in the eye. Her voice is soft.{/n} "I don't want to think about all the battles you'll have to fight... all the ways you could be killed. I... worry about you. What a strange, ridiculous feeling."

"Don't laugh. I realize how it looks — a nasty, cynical bitch transformed by the power of love. No, I know I don't deserve such a gift, but... I can try to earn it." {n}Wenduag hesitates, then says slowly,{/n} "Do you want me to change? Would you like me to act more like an uplander, and believe all that stuff about kindness, honor, and dedication? I can't promise that I'll succeed, but I can try. For you."
"I can hardly believe it myself... All my life, survival has been my only priority. But now... I don't want to survive without you."
{n}The huntress looks even more terrified than she did when you were dying in her arms. Her lips move soundlessly before she finally manages to force out the words,{/n} "Me too. I love... you."

{n}The huntress laughs as she pulls you close.{/n} "You know I don't believe in love... It's just something that uplanders invented. But..." {n}A satisfied smile appears on Wenduag's lips.{/n} "You are the most incredible person I've ever met. You're fearless, you're inspiring... See? I don't need to repeat those three stupid words. I have plenty of other words to tell you how I feel."
"I can't believe I just said that..." {n}Wenduag stares at you for a moment in stunned silence. Then she giggles happily.{/n} "But I do love you, {name}. I really do."

"But I didn't. Though I must admit, it was a close call. But I believed you were powerful enough to survive, and I was right. You passed the trial, and now we... share a bond. I wanted to open up to you before, but until you shared the poison that shaped me into who I am, you would never have been able to fully understand me. This venom in my veins would have always been a barrier between us. But now, it brings us closer together."

{n}The huntress becomes very serious.{/n} "It means that I will follow you no matter where you go, and I will fight for you until my last breath. And when the time comes for us to die, I'll cover you with my body, and I'll have no regrets. Do you hear me? I'll never regret my decision to choose you."

"Don't you see? We are special. There is no one else like us in the entire world. We're the only ones left — all the others are dead. Look into my eyes. What do you see?" {n}Wenduag brings her face close to yours, and you see yourself reflected in her huge, cat-like eyes.{/n} "When I look into your eyes, I see myself."
"It will be a miracle if we survive... but I've seen you perform plenty of miracles. I just have to trust you."
{n}Wenduag gives you an affectionate smile.{/n} "Yes. And anyone who tries to separate us will bitterly regret their mistake."

{n}The huntress shakes her head sadly.{/n} "A good chief's heart, thoughts, and life, belong to their tribe. But my heart belongs to you now, and there's nothing I can do to change that. I can no longer be a good chief to my tribe."
{n}Wenduag takes your hand. Closing her eyes, she whispers softly,{/n} "I belong to you, {name}. So I'll become whatever your heart desires. I swear."
{n}Wenduag closes her eyes wearily. She whispers softly,{/n} "Love is so sweet, but so exhausting."

"I wasn't trying to kill you. Please, you have to believe me. I would never betray you. I'm loyal to you, and I'll remain loyal forever. I swear." {n}Wenduag's voice sounds thin and fragile, like a twig frozen by the winter winds.{/n}

"How did you end up in Drezen?"
"You're an aasimar, if I'm not mistaken?"
"I have to go."

World/Dialogs/NPC_Common/VendorArsinoe/A.text: "You are a priestess of Abadar and a proponent of order in all things. Tell me, what do you think of my leadership of the crusade?"
[Devour Arsinoe] "You won't leave Drezen. No one will leave here alive."
"Is there any news about the poor folk whose souls were stolen?"
"Perhaps you've heard about the wound that sometimes opens in my chest. Are you familiar with this kind of ailment?"
"What do you think it might be?"
"Can you give me some advice on how to heal it?"
"I want you to try to heal me."
"Thank you, it all makes sense to me now."
"What are you doing here?"
"Can you help me with something before the attack?"
"I need to catch my breath."
"I'm glad that you are with us."
"I see that you have consecrated the altar of Abadar."
"I see that you have brought the altar of Abadar here to the Threshold."
"I am glad that we have a cleric of Abadar in Drezen now. I pray that the god of cities helps us protect its walls."

World/Dialogs/NPC_Common/VendorArsinoe/C.text: {n}A woman in gold-embroidered cleric's robes greets you with a polite bow. Her eyes, the color of molten gold, gleam brightly in her dusky face.{/n} "Greetings, Commander! My name is Arsinoe. I am a messenger from the temple of {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}, and I came here assuming the defenders of the fortress could use the services of a cleric."
"How can I help you?"

"My story has grown longer and longer over the years, yet, sadly, it never gets any more interesting. I was born and raised in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}. Soon I realized that bringing the word of Abadar to places where it's already been heard was too easy a challenge for a cleric like me. I have traveled all across Golarion since then, watching civilization bring enlightenment to the wildest of places. This brings joy to my heart and makes me feel like I serve my god with my deeds and not only with my words."
"That is precisely why I am here."

"The tiny barony in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} that had been my home for a very long time eventually turned into a strong and prosperous kingdom, and I felt that I had to go somewhere else and bring the blessing of Abadar to someone who really needed it. It will take quite a long time for Drezen to recover and become an unfailing stronghold once again. I will do my very best to help."

"I can sell you various divine spell scrolls. Even if you don't have anyone in your party who can read them — I'll be happy to read it for you right here. However, take care out there on your travels: a scroll is useless without someone who can read it! To use a scroll while you're on the move, you'll need a spellcaster whose magical training covers such spells, or someone skilled in magical devices."

"I'd be delighted to. Abadar is the patron deity of law, trade, and the prosperity of cities. He teaches that law and order allow civilization to develop and keep people safe and wealthy. Iomedae and Abadar are allies, since Iomedae also holds order and nobility above all else. It's hardly surprising to see so many mighty fortresses and wonderful cities in Mendev bloom under her blessing."

"Oh, yes, I am an aasimar. Hard to miss, isn't it? I look exactly like my great-great-grandmother, but I am the only one among my kin to have aasimar blood manifest so visibly in my appearance. I have to admit that it is a very fortunate coincidence: my aasimar features are rather appealing and make people trust me more easily. This is a good quality to have for a priestess wishing to gather a congregation."

"I am. Just as you are one yourself. Every time I meet another aasimar it feels like meeting family. I look exactly like my great-great-grandmother, but I am the only one among my kin to have aasimar blood manifest so visibly in my appearance. I have to admit that it is a very fortunate coincidence: my aasimar features are rather appealing and make people trust me more easily. This is a good quality to have for a priestess wishing to gather a congregation."

"That is a rather strange question indeed, but if it's an order — I will answer. There is a saying: one can't win a war and keep their gloves white, yes? I do understand that there isn't much time and energy left for landscaping when you're fighting hordes of demons to death every day, but... Abadar knows how I'd love to see Drezen neat and tidy for just one day! No missing cobbles in the street, everything sparkling clean, flowerbeds blooming, all the lawns trimmed... Glory and order instead of all this filth!"

{n}Arsinoe lowers her head respectfully.{/n} "With pleasure. I have not seen a place calmer or better organized than Drezen for some time. The Wound, evil, and chaos are outside its walls, but there is peace and order within the fortress. Everyone carries out their duties, no one is idle or lazy, and our warriors are doing their utmost to expedite our victory. I am happy to be here. To say the least."
"Abadar, I beg you, strike down this unholy beast! Don't let my death go unpunished."
{n}The aasimar looks grimly at you.{/n} "My services are still at your disposal, for this is the order of my god."

"No, but believe me, I'm not going to leave this alone. This is a serious crime, one that happened right under my nose. I consider it a personal insult and am willing to help Elan and everyone involved. Every day I spend some time trying to find the stolen souls with prayers and divine magic. My search has brought no results yet, but as soon as it does, I will let you know."
"Commander, I'm glad the Abyss did not take you."

{n}Arsinoe quickly probes you with the skill of an experienced healer.{/n} "So the wound was right here? And then it disappeared... and reappeared... Amazing! No, this is the first time I've ever heard of such magic."
"Take care of yourself, Commander."

"I'm sorry, but I do not have the right to do that. A healer who makes a blind attempt to heal a patient who is not on the verge of death is an irresponsible fool. You do not seem to be dying, so we will not take any unnecessary risks."

"I am sure that you have already used the purification and chaos-warding spells. And for obvious reasons, you do not have the option of leaving the campaign and going on a long pilgrimage to various shrines. Since that's the case... keep a diary. Make careful and systematic entries about your well-being. If it gets worse, record the circumstances under which it happens. I'm afraid this is the only advice I can offer right now."

"I think it is some kind of demonic corruption, or particles of chaos from the Abyss have entered through the wound into your body and made it so... unstable. It sounds quite interesting, incidentally. Judging from the records of researchers of the Abyss, stranger things have happened in this cursed place."
{n}Arsinoe casts a disapproving glance at the fortress.{/n} "The demons have completely neglected the fortifications here. They are in complete disarray. However, this plays right into our hands."
"I fulfill my duty to Abadar, of course. I am not afraid of chaos, so I go into a world of savagery and grief to bring the light of civilization, law, and order."
"As before, I can help you cast the necessary spells. And if you wish to recuperate, I will make sure that your rest is not disturbed."
"Rest, Commander. A hard battle lies ahead."
"May Abadar keep you, Commander."

"So I have. And before you ask me why I did this when there is a temple of Iomedae in Drezen, I will answer. Even though my god is the ally of the Inheritor, some still prefer to pray and trust in Abadar instead of her. After all, my humble altar is no worse at removing the corruption of the Abyss than the grandiose altar in the temple of Iomedae."
"The crusader army needs protection from the corruption of the Abyss, as do you, Commander. I am deeply flattered that the privilege of granting such protection has been given to me and my god."

"You wish to put my faith to the test? A reasonable request. We are surrounded by enemies who are known for their deviousness. Some cultist may try to infiltrate the defenders' ranks disguised as a cleric. So, you want me to tell you about Abadar..."

"I, in turn, am glad to see my {mf|brother|sister} in faith at the head of the crusade army. Drezen is a very special city in the eyes of Abadar. It may have been erected in honor of the Inheritor, but the Wealthy Father sees it as a relic that was lost and then retrieved. A bastion of civilization, the last frontier separating us all from the sea of chaos. I have faith that you will protect it!"
